{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZXZZqA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhC-smM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 41, "title": "Implement 8259A OCW2 programmable and rotating interrupt priority", "body": "## Problem

The PIC always arbitrates in numeric IR0–IR7 order. `Pic::pending()` and nonspecific EOI use `trailing_zeros()`, and no programmable priority or automatic-rotation state exists. Consequently, set-priority commands are ignored and rotating EOIs behave like ordinary EOIs. See [current PIC implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/5a2dbf1ea04e85ba88dfd5fe09d40f78e18db38e/src/devices.rs#L3).

This leaves a shared interrupt-delivery prerequisite incomplete across timer, keyboard and cascaded devices. Existing [PIC coverage](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/5a2dbf1ea04e85ba88dfd5fe09d40f78e18db38e/tests/core.rs#L212) checks selected fixed-priority, mask, EOI and cascade behavior; it does not establish rotating-priority support.

## Expected outcome

Implement OCW2 programmable and rotating priority independently for both PICs, integrated with existing PC-98 ports and master-IR7 cascade.

Hardware contract, from the [Intel 8259A datasheet, initialization, Figure 8 and priority/EOI sections, printed pp. 9–16](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=9):

- Lowest-priority line `L` gives highest-first order `(L+1) mod 8` through `L`. Initialization restores IR0 highest, IR7 lowest.
- Arbitration selects an unmasked request above the highest-priority active ISR bit. Nonspecific EOI clears that ISR bit; specific EOI clears the named bit.
- Decode OCW2 as follows; `n` is bits 2:0:

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `00h` | Disable rotation on automatic EOI |
| `20h` | Nonspecific EOI |
| `40h` | No operation |
| `60h+n` | Specific EOI |
| `80h` | Enable rotation on automatic EOI |
| `A0h` | Nonspecific EOI; completed line becomes lowest |
| `C0h+n` | Make line n lowest, without EOI |
| `E0h+n` | Specific EOI; line n becomes lowest |

Automatic-EOI rotation occurs on successful acknowledgement, not request arrival or status inspection. `00h` disables subsequent automatic rotation without restoring the priority order. Ordinary EOIs do not rotate. [Intel 8259A, printed pp. 13–16](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=13).

Construction and Machine reset must initialize added state deterministically to fixed priority with automatic rotation disabled; document this emulator initialization policy.

Scope is OCW2 priority behavior and its existing interrupt-path interactions. Polling, special-mask mode, special fully nested mode, general ICW sequencing/configuration, alternate cascade wiring, edge/level electrical modeling and spurious-interrupt fidelity remain separate work. Preserve the existing request and acknowledgement abstraction.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `5a2dbf1ea04e85ba88dfd5fe09d40f78e18db38e`. Supplied open-Issue inventory is empty; supplied recent improvements contain no PIC-priority implementation.

Static reproduction, derived from source and **not executed by this evaluator**:

```rust
use pc98_rust::devices::Pic;

let mut p = Pic::new(8);
p.write(true, 0);       // Unmask all lines.
p.write(false, 0xc0);   // IR0 lowest; IR1 highest.
p.request(0);
p.request(1);
assert_eq!(p.ack(), Some(9));
```

The current source selects vector 8; the expected result is vector 9.

[Bus::irq](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/5a2dbf1ea04e85ba88dfd5fe09d40f78e18db38e/src/bus.rs#L353) resolves slave requests through master IR7. Priority changes must affect each controller locally while preserving this cascade relationship.

Project progress: merged PR #40 supplies bounded Ap SMSW readback. The Coordinator reports 7 focused SMSW, 50 CPU386, 140 native integration and 54 production-Wasm browser passes in [the validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/5a2dbf1ea04e85ba88dfd5fe09d40f78e18db38e/docs/validation.md#issue-39-ap-real-mode-smsw-readback-2026-10-23). These checks were not rerun here; separate PR reviews and CI success were not supplied. SMSW does not establish protected execution or x87 support.

Retain all 26 inventory categories and their full scopes. Statuses remain: **partial** cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, keyboard, mouse, fdc, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, bios, lio, integration; **unimplemented** paging, fpu, rtc; **implemented_unverified** ide, grcg, pcm86. Completing this Issue leaves PIC partial, including the excluded modes and broader initialization/delivery acceptance above. Limited probes and six-game reports do not establish full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add original native tests, preferably `tests/pic.rs`, covering all eight programmed lowest-priority lines and every OCW2 command family. Demonstrate the reproduction fails on the unchanged baseline and passes with the implementation; record exact commands and results.
- [ ] Verify competing requests, wraparound order, masked-request retention, nested ISR blocking and nonspecific EOI after reordering. Include cases where numeric bit order differs from priority order, and verify masking an in-service line does not bypass normal-mode blocking.
- [ ] Verify rotating specific/nonspecific EOIs, set-priority without ISR clearing, ordinary EOIs without rotation, and no-op commands. Empty-ISR handling must not invent interrupts or corrupt unrelated state. Check IRR/ISR/IMR readback throughout.
- [ ] Program AEOI through the existing ICW4 path. Verify rotation enable/disable across repeated acknowledgements, no rotation from repeated `pending()`/status reads, and no automatic rotation when AEOI is disabled. Verify CPU/controller instance isolation, ICW initialization priority restoration, and Machine-reset defaults.
- [ ] Exercise both profiles through actual Bus ports: master `00h/02h`, slave `08h/0Ah`. Test competing master/slave requests, independently changed priorities, cascade ISR state, separate master/slave EOIs, and deferred delivery without lost requests.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built boot probe, offline preparation script and checked-in provenance/result manifest. Record assembler command, source/image hashes, license, exact result bytes and guards, and a maximum 2,000,000-slot budget per boot. Use no commercial ROM, guest software or copied emulator implementation.
- [ ] Boot the identical probe natively and in production release Wasm on VM and Ap, at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, before and after reset. Use existing input interfaces and guest-programmed timer/keyboard IRQs with a deterministic handshake that confirms competing IRR bits before enabling interrupts. Assert an exact delivery trace distinguishing programmed priority and rotating EOI, explicit `PIC PASS`, no `FAIL` or host error, unchanged disk bytes and bounded execution. Do not substitute host-written PASS/results or software INTs for hardware IRQ delivery. Wire fixture preparation into existing CI.
- [ ] Preserve existing PIC/cascade, timer, keyboard, DMA/FDC, CPU interrupt-shadow, HLT, GDTR/IDTR/SMSW, DOS/apps, VM and game regressions without weakening assertions or budgets. The Coordinator runs the focused PIC tests, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, media/font reproducibility checks and `npm test`, following README fixture preparation. Any alternate browser ports must preserve both projects and all assertions.
- [ ] Update hardware and validation documentation with implemented semantics, authoritative references, remaining PIC gaps and exact Coordinator/CI results, including failures or omissions. Missing evaluator-local fixtures are not a project-level blocker. Implementation, test execution, review and merge belong to the resident Coordinator; all mandatory evidence must be available before merge.
